verifications.claim: The Rooney Rule is an NFL policy established in 2003.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The policy was implemented in 2003" (R2); "Created in 2003" (R3); "established in 2003" (R6); "Instituted in 2003" (R7); "The NFL adopted the Rooney Rule in 2003" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the Rooney Rule was established or adopted in 2003 as an NFL policy.

verifications.claim: The Rooney Rule is named after former Steelers owner Dan Rooney.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "named after former Pittsburgh Steelers owner Dan Rooney" (R2); "Named after late Pittsburgh Steelers owner Dan Rooney" (R3); "named for Dan Rooney, the late owner of the Pittsburgh Steelers" (R6); "named after Dan Rooney" (R7); "named after then-chairman of the committee, Dan Rooney, the late owner of the Pittsburgh Steelers" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm it is named after Dan Rooney, former Steelers owner.

verifications.claim: Originally, the Rooney Rule required interviewing one minority candidate for head coach.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Initially, the rule applied only to head coaching candidates and required teams to interview at least one minority candidate" (R2); "The Rooney Rule originally required every NFL team with a head coaching vacancy to interview at least one diverse candidate" (R8); "The policy originally required every team with a head coaching vacancy to interview at least one or more diverse candidates" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe the original requirement as interviewing at least one minority/diverse candidate for head coach positions.

verifications.claim: The Rooney Rule now mandates interviewing at least two external minority candidates for head coaching, general manager, and coordinator vacancies.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "requires all teams to interview “two minority candidates” for head coach, general manager, and coordinator positions" (R1); "The updated policy called for teams to interview at least two minority candidates for any head coaching opening and at least one minority candidate for key coordinator positions" (R2); "requires every team to interview at least two external minority candidates for open head coach, coordinator and general manager jobs" (R3); "require clubs to interview at least two external minority candidates for head coaching openings and at least one minority candidate for any coordinator job" (R5); "Clubs must conduct an in-person interview with at least two external diverse — minority and/or female — candidates for any general manager or head-coaching opening" and "at least two minorities and/or women for all coordinator positions" (R6); "NFL teams are now required to interview at least two minority candidates for vacant head coach, GM and coordinator positions" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Current requirements explicitly match across multiple sources, including 'two external minority' for HC, GM, coordinators.

verifications.claim: The definition of diverse candidates now includes women and ethnic minorities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "In 2022, the NFL expanded the “minority candidate” definition under the Rule to include women" (R1); "Interviews for executive front office positions... were required to include at least one minority and/or female candidate" (R2); "Teams and the NFL league office must also include minorities and/or female applicants for senior-level positions" (R5); "diverse — minority and/or female" (R6); "The Rooney Rule was expanded to include women as a part of the minority candidate definition" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm current definition includes women and ethnic minorities (minorities).

verifications.claim: The Rooney Rule applies to top senior executive jobs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "one minority candidate” for QB coach and other senior executive positions" (R1); "executive front office positions—such as team president, head of football operations, general manager, and other high-ranking positions—were required to include at least one minority and/or female candidate" (R2); "one external minority candidate for senior football operations and general manager jobs" and "include minorities and/or female applicants for senior-level positions, including club president jobs" (R5); "one diverse candidate for the quarterback coach position or any senior-level executive position" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly applies to senior executive positions in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Rooney Rule requires at least one minority candidate for QB coach positions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "one minority candidate” for QB coach and other senior executive positions" (R1); "Clubs must interview a least one diverse candidate for the QB coach position" (R6); "One minority candidate is required for the QB coach position" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in sources as requiring one minority/diverse candidate for QB coach.

verifications.claim: The NFL rewards teams that develop minority talent who later become head coaches or GMs with enhanced draft picks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "rewarding third-round draft picks to those that “developed minority talent that went on to become general managers or head coaches across the league”" (R1); "rewards teams for developing minority staff by granting them compensatory draft picks if a minority coach or executive is hired away" (R3); "provide teams enhanced draft stock for hiring minority candidates as head coaches or primary football executives" (R5); "rewarding teams who developed minority talent that went on to become GMs or head coaches across the league... third-round compensatory pick" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm rewards via compensatory/enhanced draft picks for developing minority talent that becomes HC/GM.

verifications.claim: The number of Black head coaches grew from two in 2002 to higher numbers in subsequent years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "at that time, he and Edwards were the only two Black coaches in the NFL" (R2, context 2002); "There were two African American head coaches in the NFL when the Rooney Rule was put in place... Only four years later, there were seven African American head coaches" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly states two Black HCs in 2002 (when Rooney Rule put in place), increased to seven by 2006; R2 supports two in 2002.

verifications.claim: In 2026, the Florida Attorney General called the Rooney Rule "unlawful" race-and-sex discrimination.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "brazenly violates Florida law... race-and-sex-based hiring policies... The Rooney Rule and its offshoots are illegal in Florida" (R1, letter March 25, 2026); "Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier said... that the NFL’s Rooney Rule mandates hiring practices that violate Florida law... “The NFL’s use of the Rooney Rule violates Florida law by requiring race-based considerations in hiring”" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R1 letter (2026) calls it unlawful race/sex discrimination; R6 quotes AG calling it unlawful.

verifications.claim: In 2026, the Florida Attorney General threatened legal action.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Failure to provide such confirmation may result in a civil rights enforcement action" (R1); "threatening possible enforcement actions if the league doesn’t suspend the rule" (R6); "Uthmeier contends that they “require precisely what Florida law forbids”... threat of legal action implied" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly threatens enforcement action in 2026 letter; supported by R3, R6.

verifications.claim: Brian Flores is a former Dolphins coach.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Brian Flores was fired as head coach of the Miami Dolphins" (R2); "One top coordinator and former head coach, Brian Flores, is suing the NFL... Dolphins" (R3); "Brian Flores began... head coaching position by Stephen Ross, the owner of the Miami Dolphins" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm Flores as former Dolphins head coach.

verifications.claim: Former Dolphins coach Brian Flores brought a lawsuit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "in early 2022, filed a lawsuit against the NFL, the Dolphins, and two other teams alleging racial discrimination" (R2); "Brian Flores, is suing the NFL for alleged racial discrimination" (R3); "Brian Flores filed a class action lawsuit against the NFL and its thirty-two member teams" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state Flores (former Dolphins coach) filed a lawsuit against NFL/Dolphins.
